metric_units: coverage, selective error, balanced accuracy, AURC and expected calibration error (ECE, 15 equal-mass bins) are proportions in [0,1]; NLL is in nats per trial; the Brier score is the multi-class sum of squares; differences are differences of those quantities; counts of people, folds and trials are whole numbers; null means not defined, never zero
scope: Route 1 of the decision-research roadmap: selective classification and probability calibration on saved test scores of models this site already publishes. Every protocol is balanced or uniform by design, so every figure compares methods; none is a deployment error rate. No classifier was retrained, nothing extends the eight-protocol matrix, and nothing is ranked where intervals overlap.

reliable-decisions.title: Reliable decisions: when a decoder should decline to decide, and what its confidence is worth

questions.Q1: Does a threshold fixed in advance give comparable coverage and error across methods and people? (C3)
questions.Q2: Holding the classifier fixed, does a learned reject option reject errors better than the calibrated confidence? (C1, C2)
questions.Q3: Does a selective error level certified on other people's calibration data hold on new people? (C6)
questions.Q4: On EEGMAT, does LoRA adaptation of LaBraM change probability quality compared with the frozen arm of the same recipe? (C4)
questions.Q5: What does person-specific recalibration change, and how many of the new person's labels does it cost? (C5)

design.inputs: The saved test scores of models this site already publishes, on the same people and outer folds. No outer-test score was recomputed and no classifier was retrained; temperature scaling keeps the predicted label, so every full-coverage balanced accuracy equals the published one.
design.calibration_data: Participant-disjoint inner out-of-fold scores. In each outer fold the training people form four inner groups, and each group is scored by a model trained on the other three. No test person is in any calibration set. Inner models see about three quarters of the training people, so they may be less confident than the full model whose scores are tested; this approximation is part of every calibrated figure.

policies.fixed_cutoff: F: accept a trial when its calibrated top-class probability is at least 0.8 (temperature scaling fitted on the calibration scores).
policies.coverage_target: S-cov: accept the most confident trials, with the cut-off set from calibration quantiles so that 80% of trials should be accepted.
policies.risk_certification: S-risk: selection with guaranteed risk (SGR, delta 0.05) on the calibration scores, certifying a selective error no higher than r*, here the relative target: half the calibration error. A fold where nothing can be certified accepts nothing.
policies.learned_reject: L: an L2 logistic selector on the raw top-1 and top-2 scores and their margin, plus 16 principal components of a model-independent spectral descriptor (C = 1, untuned), trained on the calibration scores to predict which trials the classifier gets wrong.
policies.ranking: S ranks trials by calibrated top-class probability, L by the selector. Error at a test coverage takes the most confident share of the test trials under that ranking, so it measures the ranking alone.
policies.recalibration: R0: the population temperature, no label from the new person. R1: a personal temperature fitted on a labelled prefix of the new person's own trials. R-unl: the population temperature, with only the coverage cut-off re-set from the same prefix, unlabelled. All three are scored on the same remaining trials.

design.uncertainty: Paired participant-cluster bootstrap over the test people of a protocol: 2,000 resamples, seed 20261002, 95% percentile intervals, the same resampled people for every method, policy and arm. No multiplicity correction.
design.wording_rule: A contrast is called a difference only when its paired 95% interval excludes 0; otherwise "no difference resolved". No ranking where intervals overlap. Descriptive levels are never called differences.
design.zero_accepted: A policy that accepts nothing has no error rate: null, never zero.
design.freeze: The protocol was frozen and amended once (A1) before any stage-1 computation. Thresholds, temperatures and selectors were written and hashed before scoring; outer-test labels were masked during stage 1; nothing was selected by test results; degenerate fits were flagged and kept.

reliable-decisions.protocol_amendment: A1 (2026-10-04, after stage 0, before any stage-1 fit): wording rule restricted to genuine differences, C3 pairwise differences added, person percentiles need >= 20 people with a defined value

seeds.description: Every saved secondary seed of the trained methods, each with its own cross-fit, temperature, cut-offs and selector, scored on that seed's saved test predictions. Seeds are never treated as people; no contrast is drawn between seeds or with the primary row.

matched_model_holdout.description: The base model is trained on three quarters of the training people and calibrated on the remaining quarter, so calibration and test scores come from one model. Its accuracy differs from the site's and is not published.
matched_model_holdout.published: risk-certification fold counts only; never an accuracy

map_sensitivity.description: Platt scaling (two classes) or vector scaling (BETA) in place of temperature scaling, on the same calibration scores. These maps can change the predicted label, so their accuracy is not the site's and is not published.
map_sensitivity.published: risk-certification fold counts only; never an accuracy

l_joint.description: Exploratory. A SelectiveNet-style EEGNet (alpha 0.5, lambda 32, target coverage 0.8) trained with its own selection head g. Within the same model, g is compared with the calibrated confidence of its own classifier head; positive means g is worse. It changes the classifier, so its accuracy is not the site's and is not published here, and it is never compared with the primary learned-reject contrasts.

all_protocols: Every protocol in this route is balanced or uniform by design (EEGMAT 1:1, BETA uniform over 40 targets, mi-rest balanced, idle cue-gated with equal idle and command windows). The numbers compare methods; none of them is a deployment error rate, and class-conditional rows are given so that readers can re-weight to another prevalence.
A risk-coverage curve exists only where something is accepted. At zero coverage there is no error rate, not a zero one; fewer than 10 accepted trials is flagged unstable.

A certified selective risk (S-risk, SGR with delta 0.05) assumes that calibration and test data are exchangeable. Across people they are not, so S-risk is a nominal guarantee: its failure rate is measured here, not assumed.

Rejecting likely errors on known classes is not detecting unfamiliar input. An uncertainty threshold may not flag an unseen class (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13324). Route 1 makes no out-of-distribution claim.

The idle protocol is cue-gated and about three minutes per test phase. It gives per-window proportions at each decision time only, never a false-activation rate per hour, and these route-1 window proportions are a different unit from the site's existing trial-level idle figures; do not compare or merge them.

Calibration data are participant-disjoint inner out-of-fold scores (cross-fit). Inner models see about 3/4 of the training people, so they may be less confident than the full model whose scores are tested. This approximation is part of every calibrated figure.

Full-coverage balanced accuracy equals the site value for every primary method, because temperature scaling keeps the predicted label. Matched-model holdout, map-sensitivity and L-joint rows use different models or maps and must not be mixed with site accuracies.

A contrast is called a difference only when its paired 95% participant-bootstrap interval excludes 0 (no multiplicity correction); otherwise "no difference resolved". No ranking where intervals overlap. Descriptive entries are never called differences.
